event.title: Alberta votes on a non-binding separation question
event.what_happened: Albertans are voting on Question 10 of a provincial referendum: whether Alberta should remain a province of Canada or whether the provincial government should begin the constitutional process needed to hold a later binding referendum on separation. The vote itself is non-binding, ballots are being counted by hand, and the separation question is scheduled to be counted first.
who: pro-separation campaigners including the Alberta Prosperity Project and Pathway to Independence
event.event_date_basis: Packet 4 says, "So please vote on this and the other 9 referendum questions on October 19th." Packet 7 says Smith said Alberta would not hold another separation referendum if this one fails "on Oct. 19."

latest_development.summary: Voting began Monday on Alberta's non-binding separation question. Elections officials are to count ballots by hand, with Question 10 counted first; counting starts no earlier than 20:00 local and BBC reports results are expected in the early hours of Tuesday.

confirmed_facts.fact: Albertans are voting on Oct. 19 on a choice question asking whether Alberta should remain a province of Canada or whether the Government of Alberta should begin the legal process required under the Canadian Constitution to hold a binding provincial referendum on separation.
The result of Question 10 is not binding.
Question 10 is one of 10 referendum questions on the ballot, and it is the only choice question; Questions 1-9 are yes/no questions.
Elections Alberta says ballots will be counted by hand and Question 10 will be counted first.

BBC reports officials have up to 48 hours to complete the count, starting no earlier than 20:00 local on Monday, and says the separation-question results should be available in the early hours of Tuesday.
Premier Danielle Smith says she opposes separation and will vote to keep Alberta in Canada.
Prime Minister Mark Carney campaigned for a vote to keep Alberta in Canada and warned against using the referendum as a mere message to Ottawa.
A court blocked or quashed the pro-separation petition after arguments that First Nations had not been properly consulted; the ruling is being appealed.
Elections Alberta validated the citizen-led pro-separation petition on July 24, saying it had verified nearly 223,000 signatures out of almost 280,000 valid names counted.
A separate anti-separation petition gathered more than 400,000 signatures, according to BBC's reporting.
As of Thursday night, Elections Alberta said more than one million ballots had been cast in advance voting or by mail, according to CP24/Canadian Press.
Fox News reported that as of Saturday, more than 1.2 million Albertans had cast a ballot.

chronology.event: Elections Alberta says Alberta entered a referendum period; third-party advertising rules took effect for referendum questions already in period.
Elections Alberta says the referendum period for Question 10, the separation question, began.

Elections Alberta validated the pro-separation citizen petition, with nearly 223,000 signatures verified out of almost 280,000 valid names counted, while the petition remained tied up in court on appeal.
Carney spoke at a pro-Canada rally in Calgary, warning against a vote meant only to 'send a message' to Ottawa.
Carney delivered remarks at the Forever Canadian Rally in Edmonton; Angus Reid Institute released referendum-related polling the same day.
On the eve of the vote, separatist organizer Chris Scott told BBC the campaign had already achieved some of its goals regardless of the result.
Albertans began voting on the non-binding separation question and nine other referendum questions.
Counting is to begin no earlier than 20:00 local, with Question 10 counted first.
BBC reports results on the separation question are expected in the early hours of Tuesday.

background.fact: Earlier in 2026, Danielle Smith called the vote after petitions for and against separation gathered large support; BBC describes roughly 300,000 signatures on the pro-separation petition and more than 400,000 on an opposing petition.
Last year, Smith's government made it easier to start referendums, according to Al Jazeera's reporting.
The referendum debate has been divisive even though polling cited by BBC and Fox suggested most Albertans would choose to remain in Canada.

legal.statement: Voters are deciding a non-binding choice question: remain a province of Canada or have the Alberta government commence the legal process required under the Canadian Constitution to hold a binding provincial referendum on separation.
If the option to begin the process wins, the government says it would start the legal processes necessary to hold a binding referendum on separation at a later date.
A court decision found that a binding referendum on separation could not be held without a constitutionally mandated consultation process with First Nations about effects on treaty rights.

lifecycle.event: Alberta referendum Question 10 on whether Alberta should remain in Canada or begin the legal process for a future binding separation referendum
lifecycle.notes: Ballots are counted by hand; Question 10 is counted first; BBC says counting starts no earlier than 20:00 local on Oct. 19 and officials have up to 48 hours to complete the task.

reconciled.discrepancy: Advance-vote totals of 'over one million' and 'more than 1.2 million' appear different.
reconciled.resolution: They refer to the same category at different as-of times: over one million as of Thursday night, and more than 1.2 million as of Saturday.
reconciled.resolved_by: Packet 9 gives the Thursday-night as-of; Packet 2 gives the Saturday as-of.

reconciled.discrepancy: The pro-separation petition is described as having about 300,000 signatures in BBC, but Global reports nearly 223,000 verified out of almost 280,000 valid names counted.
reconciled.resolution: These are different stages/categories of petition measurement: approximate signatures gathered, valid names counted, and verified signatures. They are not a direct contradiction.
reconciled.resolved_by: Packet 8 distinguishes verified signatures from valid names counted; Packet 1 gives an approximate gathered figure.

reconciled.discrepancy: Some coverage frames Monday's vote as deciding separation, while official materials say it is a non-binding question about whether to begin the legal process toward a future binding referendum.
reconciled.resolution: Elections Alberta's official referendum page states the result on Question 10 is not binding and sets out the wording focused on commencing a legal process toward a later binding referendum.

unverified: Fox reports that Alberta separatist leaders met Republican strategists in Calgary in January and separately suggested exchanging water and oil for U.S. support in meetings with State Department officials last year; no other packet here independently corroborates those claims.

Fox's report says more than half of the UCP's nearly 55,000 members support Alberta's independence, attributing the point to Cory Morgan; no independent supporting packet here confirms that membership figure or level of support.

Fox's opening reference to Alberta mourning four soldiers killed and dozens injured in a fire at a military base is unrelated to this referendum event and is not corroborated elsewhere in this packet set.

angle: Albertans are voting today on a non-binding separation question that would tell the provincial government whether to begin the constitutional process for a later binding independence referendum, with hand-counted results expected early Tuesday.
